_comment: 'suppressions' entries silence one finding kind for one function. Use them for
deliberate editorial choices, not to hide real drift — e.g. a page that shows one
representative overload on purpose rather than all twelve widths of abs().
Each entry: {function, kind, reason} and optionally 'versions' (a list of
major.minor strings). Omit 'versions' for a suppression that holds on every branch,
mirroring the scoping convention in sql_verify_suppressions.json.
'name_aliases' maps a doc page stem to the function name registered in
gensrc/script/functions.py, for pages named differently from the registered
function or documenting a group of related functions on one page.
Both start empty on purpose: the first run's report is the input to filling them in,
and an entry added without a reason is indistinguishable from hidden drift.
